{{Short description|Theorem}}
'''Komlós' theorem''' is a theorem from [[probability theory]] and [[mathematical analysis]] about the [[Cesàro summation|Cesàro convergence]] of a [[subsequence]] of [[random variable]]s (or [[Function (mathematics)|function]]s) and their subsequences to an [[Lp space|integrable]] random variable (or function). It's also an existence theorem for an integrable random variable (or function). There exist a probabilistic and an analytical version for [[Finite measure|finite]] [[measure space]]s.

The theorem was proven in 1967 by [[János Komlós (mathematician)|János Komlós]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=János Komlós|date=1967|doi=10.1007/BF02020976|issue=1|journal=Acta Mathematica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae|title=A Generalisation of a Problem of Steinhaus|volume=18}}</ref> There exists also a generalization from 1970 by [[Srishti D. Chatterji]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=S. D. Chatterji|date=1970|doi=10.1007/BF01404326|pages=235–245|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|title=A general strong law|volume=9}}</ref>

== Komlós' theorem ==
=== Probabilistic version ===
Let <math>(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)</math> be a [[probability space]] and <math>\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots</math> be a sequence of real-valued random variables defined on this space with <math>\sup\limits_{n}\mathbb{E}[|\xi_n|]<\infty.</math>

Then there exists a random variable <math>\psi\in L^1(P)</math> and a subsequence <math>(\eta_k)=(\xi_{n_{k}})</math>, such that for every arbitrary subsequence <math>(\tilde{\eta}_n)=(\eta_{k_{n}})</math> when <math>n\to \infty</math> then
:<math>\frac{(\tilde{\eta}_1+\cdots +\tilde{\eta}_n)}{n}\to \psi</math>
<math>P</math>-[[almost surely]].

=== Analytic version ===
Let <math>(E,\mathcal{A},\mu)</math> be a finite measure space and <math>f_1,f_2,\dots</math> be a sequence of real-valued functions in <math>L^1(\mu)</math> and <math>\sup\limits_n \int_E |f_n|\mathrm{d}\mu<\infty</math>. Then there exists a function <math>\upsilon \in L^1(\mu)</math> and a subsequence <math>(g_k)=(f_{n_{k}})</math> such that for every arbitrary subsequence
<math>(\tilde{g}_n)=(g_{k_{n}})</math> if <math>n\to \infty</math> then
:<math>\frac{(\tilde{g}_1+\cdots +\tilde{g}_n)}{n}\to \upsilon </math>
<math>\mu</math>-[[almost everywhere]].

=== Explanations ===
So the theorem says, that the sequence <math>(\eta_k)</math> and all its subsequences converge in Césaro.
